`.skilled/hooks/hook-flags.env` is **gitignored** — [SOURCE: .gitignore:354] (`.opencode/hooks/hook-flags.env`) and [SOURCE: .gitignore:355] (`.skilled/hooks/hook-flags.env`). A gitignored file is never present in a GitHub Actions checkout, so no CI job can read it. Using it would mean the switch silently does nothing on the runner — the worst failure mode for a control.
`vars` and `env` are **not** available in `on.push`/`on.pull_request` filters (no context is available there).
A workflow can therefore never be prevented from *triggering* by a variable. It can only be prevented from *doing work*.

The committed sibling is the example — [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/hook-flags.env.example:1] states the rule: copy to the local name and uncomment what you want OFF. `.env.example` is the one env file the ignore rules re-include: [SOURCE: .gitignore:30] (`!.env.example`).

The shape worth copying: **committed example, gitignored local override, everything ON by default, environment wins over file**. That is precisely the semantics a CI control needs, and `vars.*` reproduces it on GitHub's side: an unset repository variable resolves to an empty string, so a condition written as `vars.X != 'off'` evaluates TRUE and the job runs (expression semantics — **inferred** from the empty-string resolution of an undefined `vars` lookup; the default-on property is what matters and it is also the safer direction if my inference is wrong, since an error would fail the run rather than skip it silently).
[SOURCE: .env.example:275] states the precedence rule the shape should copy: "May also be set in .skilled/hooks/hook-flags.env (a real env var wins)."

[SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/hook-flags.env.example:55] — "CI never reads this file, so the repository's own checks stay on there." That is a direct statement that the hook flag file is a local-only surface, by design.
**`dependabot-auto-merge` gets no switch.** It is safety-relevant and one job; putting it behind a variable buys nothing and risks a silent auto-merge change.

**`off` is the only disable token.** `vars.X != 'off'` runs the job for `0`, `false`, `no`, `disabled` and typos alike. That is deliberately fail-safe (a mistake leaves the gate on), and it must be documented, because someone will otherwise set `SKILLED_CI_TESTS=0`, see the suites still run, and conclude the switch is broken.

**AND, never replace.** Where a job already has an event condition, the switch is added to it and both are parenthesised: `if: ${{ (vars.SKILLED_CI != 'off') && (!endsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'Trigger-Index-Rebuild: ci')) }}`. Replacing the existing condition would silently drop the loop guard. This is the one place a scoped edit can regress behaviour, so it deserves a review rule of its own.

**No `${{ }}` wrapper.** A bare job-level `if:` is already an expression, which is how the four existing conditions are written — e.g. [SOURCE: .github/workflows/trigger-index-rebuild.yml:33]. Adding braces would be a stylistic difference with no behaviour change, so match the tree.

**The switch sits above `permissions:` and `runs-on:`**, so a reader sees the on/off state before the least-privilege block. Note 12 of the 33 workflows have no top-level `permissions:` at all; that is a separate hygiene item (angle 8), not something this gate introduces.

The committed sibling `.env.example` is a *documentation template*: its rows are commented-out definitions, e.g. [SOURCE: .env.example:110] (`# SPECKIT_STOP_HOOK_ORPHAN_SWEEP=off`) and [SOURCE: .env.example:162], whose only uncommented rows are the empty secret placeholders of section 1, e.g. [SOURCE: .env.example:58]. A parser reading it would read comments and empty strings. It is the human-readable index, not a machine-read config.
